Hi Elena —

Thanks for the requirements doc. Quick commercial/contract note and an initial draft approach below. Attaching a Word draft of the TPS annex for procurement to review.

Commercial summary (high level):
- Additional reserved capacity: +6 A100-eq GPUs (monthly reserved fee).
- Tokens/sec commitment: Baseline guaranteed throughput = 28,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool (measured as aggregated sustained TPS over a 10-minute sliding window). Burst allowance: 40,000 tokens/sec for sustained bursts up to 2 minutes, with automated bursting to a shared overflow pool thereafter.
- Credits & cap: Service credits accrue for breaches of the baseline SLO when sustained for >10 minutes. Credits capped at 30% of monthly reservation fee per billing period.

Annex language notes (summary):
- Measurement: TPS measured at the platform ingress after pre-routing and batching but before tokenization metadata; windowing and aggregation rules documented in Section 2 of the annex.
- SLO & breach definition: Breach = observed aggregated sustained TPS below baseline for >10 minutes, or P95 latency exceedance >X ms for >5 minutes (we'll fill X based on target model mix).
- Fallbacks: Auto-fallback to a warm-compatible quantized variant (same family) if the primary model cannot be served within SLO due to capacity constraints. Fallback not to impact customer data routing (no cross-tenant requests).
- Term: Annex mirrors renewal term; modifications require 30 days' notice.

I attached the draft: "Redwood_TPS_Annex_Draft_20270924.docx". If that looks broadly OK, we'll update the specific latency P95 numbers after Rishi confirms model-level targets.

Folks —

Technical clarifications on the TPS SLO and fallback behavior, so procurement understands operational limits: 

- Pool-level measurement: The TPS baseline (28k) will be measured across the dedicated pool attached to Aperture's account. We recommend measuring over 10-minute sliding windows with 1-minute sampling.
- Burst behavior: 40k burst is achievable if KV cache hit rates stay >85% and average sequence lengths don't exceed 512 tokens. For workloads with lower cache hit or longer sequences, effective TPS drops; we'll include guidance in the annex.
- Autoscaling & warm pools: We can offer a warm-hot buffer (1–2 GPUs kept in warm state) to reduce cold-start impact. Warm buffer adds cost; Neha can include pricing.
- Fallback model list: Primary: aper_v2 (high quality), Fallback A: aper_v2-quant (4-bit), Fallback B: aper_v1-optimized (smaller). We will guarantee that fallbacks preserve request routing and token accounting but may change output distribution — customers should pin critical prompts to primary models if determinism is required.
- Operational playbook: On sustained breach we will: 1) Notify customer; 2) Trigger autoscale/burst; 3) If autoscale fails, shift traffic to fallback variants with a concurrency cap.

I'm attaching a capacity-mapping workbook mapping expected TPS by model family and sequence length (capacity-mapping.xlsx) and a short CSV that lists compatibility of common apertures models (tps-model-compatibility.csv).

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-mapping.xlsx, tps-model-compatibility.csv
